merged.finding: ARCH AD-16 calls the fixture header words PROPOSED and attributes them to T50, but the spec fixes those exact words and T50 pins a different, separate per-render marking that ARCH never mentions. An implementer following ARCH renders only the header and fails T50.
merged.evidence: ARCH:166 "header reads `SYNTHETIC FIXTURE <variant>, not Orca data` (T50; exact words PROPOSED)"; acceptance-tests.md:44 T50 "each carry \"synthetic fixture, not live evidence\"".
merged.reason: False claim (spec-fixed words labelled PROPOSED, wrong test cited) that drops a T50 requirement; UX (EXPERIENCE.md:64, :215, :298) already separates the two, so ARCH also contradicts UX.
merged.fix: In AD-16 replace "(T50; exact words PROPOSED)" with "(rendering-rules.md:17, spec-fixed)" and add: "Separately, every R0 render of A, B and C carries the T50 marking `synthetic fixture, not live evidence` (acceptance-tests.md:44)." Apply the same edit to the identical copy _bmad-output/specs/spec-orca-observer/ARCHITECTURE-SPINE.md.

merged.finding: ARCH AD-13 reduces the under-80 screen to the notice and the COUNTS strip only, which drops the question-source gap notice the spec requires at every width and contradicts the UX under-80 row (notice above the COUNTS strip plus the ledger short form at the reduced width).
merged.evidence: ARCH:148 "below 80 `terminal too narrow (min 80)` and the COUNTS strip only"; rendering-rules.md:31 "Above the ledger, at every width, the gap notice"; EXPERIENCE.md:108 "short form at the reduced width".
merged.reason: Contradiction with the spec (rendering-rules.md:12, :31) and with the higher-ranked UX document; the narrow screen would lose the R1 UNVERIFIED notice required by owner decision 1.
merged.fix: In AD-13 replace "below 80 `terminal too narrow (min 80)` and the COUNTS strip only" with "below 80 `terminal too narrow (min 80)` above the COUNTS strip, whose denominators still print, with the gap notice kept (rendering-rules.md:12, :31) and the ledger in its short form at the reduced width (EXPERIENCE.md:108)". Apply the same edit to the spec-folder copy.

merged.finding: ARCH's CD-6 default (repeated in AD-20 at ARCH:190 and the operational envelope at ARCH:238) makes `e` show `export disabled` and skips every live snapshot write until UX-OQ-4 is decided. The spec requires `e` to write the record export (T27, SPEC.md:57) and a snapshot each R1 cycle (SPEC.md:59, prd.md:235 FR-16), and UX has `e` write the export (EXPERIENCE.md:266).
merged.evidence: ARCH:300 "`e` shows `export disabled (destination undecided)` and each live snapshot write is skipped and counted"; acceptance-tests.md:19 "T27: `e`/`--once` writes the record export".
merged.reason: The default disables behaviour pinned by T27 and FR-16, contradicting spec, PRD and UX; the defect is the default, not the fact that UX-OQ-4 (destination) is open.
merged.fix: Change the CD-6 default to a PROPOSED destination (a per-user state directory, `~/.local/state/superclaude/observe/`): `e` writes a timestamped text export there and each live cycle atomically replaces one snapshot file there, both replaceable when the owner settles UX-OQ-4; remove "skipped and counted" and `export disabled (destination undecided)` from CD-6, AD-20 (ARCH:190) and the operational envelope (ARCH:238), and apply the same edits to the spec-folder copy.

merged.finding: UX and ARCH carry contradictory defaults for the same open question (UX-OQ-8 / CD-16): ARCH names the shared `worktreeId` on each ledger row, UX names it only in the inspector and the text export. T20 requires two rows each naming it, so the UX default would fail the acceptance test; the spec ledger column list (rendering-rules.md:29) does not list a worktree column but does not forbid one (it forbids only a `stage` column).
merged.evidence: acceptance-tests.md:17 T20 "two sessions sharing one `worktreeId` as two rows each naming it"; EXPERIENCE.md:243 "PROPOSED: each row's inspector and the plain-text export name the full `resource.worktreeId`".
merged.reason: Contradiction between documents; UX, though ranked above ARCH, is wrong against its own source T20 (acceptance-tests.md:17), so the UX default is the one to change, and ARCH CD-16 already states the T20 default while keeping the question open.
merged.fix: At EXPERIENCE.md:243 change the PROPOSED default to "each ledger row names its `resource.worktreeId` (or `worktree unknown`), as T20 requires (acceptance-tests.md:17); the inspector and text export also name it in full; where the row shows it and how it behaves at each width is open (UX-OQ-8)", and at EXPERIENCE.md:531 change "This document names it in the inspector and export only (PROPOSED)" to "Default: the row names it per T20 (PROPOSED placement); column placement and width-class behaviour are open". Leave UX-OQ-8 open.

merged.finding: PRD FR-8 says the ledger's finished-traversal mismatch string is pinned by T47, but T47 tests only the question area; no acceptance test (T4, T16, T18, T35, T38, T42, T47 checked) pins the ledger form `collected n / reported T (mismatch)`.
merged.evidence: prd.md:174 "`collected n / reported T (mismatch)` (rendering-rules.md), pinned by T47"; acceptance-tests.md:41 T47 "Before QUESTION-OBSERVATION the question area reads...".
merged.reason: False claim of test coverage in a testable-consequences list; the ledger mismatch form is untested, and the PRD hides that.
merged.fix: At prd.md:174 replace "(rendering-rules.md), pinned by T47" with "(rendering-rules.md:55); no acceptance test pins the ledger form yet (T47 covers only the question-area mismatch note)".
